Jamie Raskin Jeffrey Epstein DOJ — the October 21 letter, read from the document itself.

On October 21, 2026, Rep. Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, wrote to Attorney General Todd Blanche and Vaughn Ary, director of DOJ's Office of International Affairs. The four-page letter makes two demands, quoted verbatim in this reel:

1. Every record of foreign Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty requests for DOJ help investigating potential Epstein co-conspirators.
2. Every record of DOJ's decisions to deny or oppose cooperation requests from state and local investigators.

Raskin alleges — his word is "obstructing" — that DOJ is blocking Britain's investigation into Peter Mandelson and New Mexico's Zorro Ranch investigation. New Mexico AG Raúl Torrez says his office's request for the unredacted files was "stonewalled"; the state says it eventually received 31 pages, much of it news clippings. New Mexico sued DOJ over the files in August; DOJ moved to dismiss in October, saying victim privacy and court orders limit what it can share. No DOJ response to this letter itself has been located yet.

It is an oversight demand — not a subpoena, not a charge, not a finding. The deadline in the letter: 5:00 p.m., November 4, 2026.

EpsteinWiki has a knowledge-base page on the inquiry. The full letter is in the archive: https://grokarchivehub.com

Shawn Ryan, Peter Thiel, and the names she says she wasn't allowed to say.

Researcher Leah (@leahfiles) says she was booked on the Shawn Ryan Show to follow the money on TPUSA and the surveillance state — and told, right before filming, not to name Andreessen Horowitz or Peter Thiel. Her post attaches Ryan's own LinkedIn, which lists him as an investor in Anduril Industries (Oct 2025–present) and Shield AI (Nov 2025–present). Public record: Thiel's Founders Fund led Anduril's $2.5B round in June 2025; Andreessen Horowitz co-led its $5B round in May 2026. The episode never aired. The naming ban is her allegation; the listing is his document.

Why it's in our lane: Peter Thiel is a documented figure in the Epstein record. Epstein pitched Thiel's fund, Valar, on Ehud Barak's Reporty in 2015, and in February 2016 Barak described courting seniors of "a new Investment Fund owned by Peter Thiel and JE" (Barak leak 28568).
